memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'When we went back to your servant my father, we told him what my lord had said. Then our father said, "Go back and buy a little more food." But we said, "We cannot go down. Only if our youngest brother is with us will we go. We cannot see the man's face unless our youngest brother is with us."'" — Gen 44:24-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"We cannot see the man's face unless our youngest brother is with us."

The condition was absolute. There was no negotiating it, no clever workaround, no partial obedience that would do. Either Benjamin came, or there would be no meeting and no food. Jacob could delay it — and he did, for a while — but hunger eventually made the decision for him.

There is a spiritual echo here worth sitting with. There is one condition for seeing the face of God, and it too is absolute. No one comes to the Father except through the Son (Jn 14:6). We cannot arrive with our own credentials, our religious effort, our sincerity or our good record. We come with Christ, or we do not come.

That sounds narrow, and it is. But it is also the kindest news in the world, because it means access does not depend on how well we have performed. It depends entirely on Him — and He is enough.

Jacob resisted because he was afraid of losing something precious. In the end, sending Benjamin was how he got everything back, including the son he thought was dead. Surrendering to God's terms always costs us something. It never costs us as much as we feared, and it always gives back more than we gave.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there something God has clearly asked of you that you have been delaying?
2. What does it mean to you that access to God rests on Christ and not on your performance?
3. What have you been afraid to surrender to Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that I can come to You through Jesus and not through my own record. Help me stop delaying what You have asked of me, and trust that Your terms are always good. Amen.
